questions.q: What is the independent variable conventionally plotted on in a scientific line graph?
Which axis on a line graph is used for plotting the dependent variable that responds to changes?
What does a straight line of best fit passing through the origin (0, 0) on a graph indicate about two variables?
a: They are directly proportional to each other.

questions.q: How do you calculate the gradient (slope) of a straight-line graph?
a: Multiply change in x by change in y
Divide the change in y (rise) by the change in x (run)

questions.q: What does a steep gradient on a distance-time graph represent?
a: A higher speed or rate of motion

questions.q: What does a horizontal flat line on a distance-time graph signify about an object's motion?
a: It is moving at constant high speed.

questions.q: When drawing a line of best fit for scattered experimental points, how should the line be positioned?
a: Connecting the first and last point in a sharp zigzag
Drawn vertically from top to bottom
Passing as close as possible to all points, with a balanced number of points on either side

questions.q: What does the area under a speed-time graph represent physically?
a: Total distance traveled by the object

questions.q: What does a curved line sloping upwards on a speed-time graph indicate?
Why is it important to use more than half of the available grid space on graph paper when plotting scientific data?
a: To make the graph clear, easy to read, and allow accurate interpolation and gradient calculation
To make the axes lines thicker

questions.q: What is interpolation on a graph?
a: Guessing values far outside the measured data range
Estimating unknown values between measured data points on the graph

questions.q: What is extrapolation on a graph?
a: Extending the line of best fit beyond the measured data points to predict unmeasured values

questions.q: What does a negative correlation (inverse relationship) look like on a scatter graph?
a: A straight or curved line sloping downwards from left to right
A line sloping upwards from left to right

questions.q: On a force-extension graph for a spring, what does the gradient of the straight linear section represent?
a: The mass of the weight hanger
The spring constant (stiffness of the spring)

questions.q: What does a constant positive gradient on a speed-time graph indicate?
Why must axis labels on a scientific graph always include both the quantity name and its unit (e.g., Force / N)?
a: To ensure clarity and allow correct interpretation of the plotted values

How can you find the speed of an object at a specific instant from a curved distance-time graph?
a: Draw a tangent to the curve at that point and calculate its gradient
Calculate the area under the curve

questions.q: What does a scatter graph with points showing no clear pattern or trend indicate?
a: No correlation or relationship between the two variables

questions.q: When plotting points on graph paper, what symbol is standard practice for marking each data point?
a: Small, neat crosses (X) or sharp dots (.)

questions.q: What does a non-linear curve on a current-voltage graph for a filament lamp indicate about its resistance?
a: Resistance is changing (increasing as current and temperature rise)

questions.q: If the graph of variable A against variable B is a straight line that does not pass through the origin (has a y-intercept), what does this prove?
a: Variable A is zero when B is zero.
Variable A is directly proportional to variable B.
Variable A is linearly related to variable B, but they are not directly proportional.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of drawing a line of best fit rather than connecting every dot with jagged lines?
a: To make the graph look artistic
To show the general underlying trend while smoothing out random experimental errors

questions.q: What does a straight line sloping downwards from left to right on a distance-time graph represent?
a: An object moving backward towards its starting position at constant speed

questions.q: How should scale intervals on graph axes be chosen when setting up grid paper?
a: Using simple, easy-to-divide scales like multiples of 1, 2, or 5 (avoiding awkward divisions like 3 or 7)
Using whatever spacing fits the first three numbers
Making the x-axis scale different for every single grid square

Which of the following describes a direct proportion relationship between two variables, x and y?
a: As x increases, y decreases exponentially.
As x increases, y stays completely constant.
As x increases, y increases at a constant rate, and the graph is a straight line through the origin.

questions.q: What should be done with an obvious outlier (anomalous point) when drawing a line of best fit on a graph?
a: Ignore the outlier, do not let it influence the line, and exclude it from gradient calculations
Force the line of best fit to bend sharply to touch it
Make it the origin point of the graph
